title: Sunny and the Spring Blossoms | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka walks under a wattle tree in full bloom at night and stands in a shower of tiny golden flowers so light they drift down like warm snowflakes. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The wattle tree was in full bloom.

Sunny smelled it before she saw it — that sweet, warm, powdery smell that meant spring had arrived and the wattle knew it. She followed the smell and found the tree — a cloud of tiny golden blooms, each cluster smaller than her paw, but there were thousands of them.

A breeze moved through.

The flowers fell.

Not all at once — just a drift, a shower of tiny golden things coming down through the moonlight. They were so light they barely fell. They floated. They took their time, each one a small soft star descending slowly through the dark air.

Sunny held out her paws.

Blossoms landed on them. Blossoms landed on her nose. On her ears. She looked down and her golden-brown fur was covered in tiny golden flowers.

She laughed quietly.

She was a wattle quokka.

She sat down under the tree and waited for another breeze.

When it came, the blossoms fell again — a golden shower in the moonlight, landing in her fur, on the ground, on her upturned face.

The smell was warm and sweet.

The falling flowers were warm and sweet.

Everything was warm and sweet and slow.

She lay back in the carpet of fallen blossoms.

Spring had arrived, and she was part of it.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, spring blossoms. Goodnight, little one.
